name: MonarchStepper
title: Stepper
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row and Column of drawn step markers, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints with androidx.compose.ui.text.TextMeasurer for the automatic compact form, Modifier.clickable for reached steps, MonarchProgress (androidx.compose.material3.LinearProgressIndicator) in the compact form
summary: Multi-step progress for wizards, onboarding and setup flows: a row or a column of numbered steps, or a compact "Step 2 of 5" with a progress bar.
whenToUse: At the top of a multi-step flow (horizontal, which becomes compact on a phone) or beside it on a wide screen (vertical). Pass onSelect to let people go back to steps they have reached.
whenNotToUse: Not for the progress of a task that runs by itself; use MonarchProgress. Not for sections the user can visit in any order; use Material 3 tabs (PrimaryTabRow). Not for changing a number; that is a different control.
api: @Composable fun MonarchStepper(steps: List<MonarchStepperStep>, current: Int, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, furthest: Int? = null, orientation: MonarchStepperOrientation = MonarchStepperOrientation.Horizontal, compact: MonarchStepperCompactMode = MonarchStepperCompactMode.Automatic, onSelect: ((step: MonarchStepperStep, index: Int) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchStepperLabels = MonarchStepperLabels(), finished: Boolean = false, busy: Boolean = false)

@Composable fun MonarchStepper(steps: List<MonarchStepperStep>, currentId: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, furthestId: String? = null, orientation: MonarchStepperOrientation = MonarchStepperOrientation.Horizontal, compact: MonarchStepperCompactMode = MonarchStepperCompactMode.Automatic, onSelect: ((step: MonarchStepperStep, index: Int) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchStepperLabels = MonarchStepperLabels(), finished: Boolean = false, busy: Boolean = false)
class MonarchStepperStep(id: String, label: String, description: String? = null, optional: Boolean = false, complete: Boolean = false, error: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true)
enum class MonarchStepperCompactMode { Automatic, Always, Never }

class MonarchStepperLabels(progress: String? = null, stepOf: ((step: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, complete: String? = null, error: String? = null, current: String? = null, optional: String? = null, busy: String? = null)

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps, in order. Each has an id, a label, and optionally a description and the flags optional, complete, error and enabled. No steps draws nothing.

options.name: current / currentId
options.description: The current step, by position from 0 or by identifier. Steps before it are complete. A position outside the steps is moved inside; an unknown identifier selects the first step.

options.name: furthest / furthestId
options.description: The furthest step the user has reached, when they have gone back. Steps up to it stay selectable. By default, and when it is before the current step, the current step.

options.name: compact
options.description: Automatic shows the compact form when the steps of a horizontal stepper do not fit the width with each name on one line; Always and Never fix the form.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes reached steps (complete ones and any up to furthest, except the current and disabled ones) buttons. Receives the step and its position.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: "Progress", "Step 2 of 5", "completed", "needs attention", "current step" and "Optional".

options.name: finished
options.description: Every step is done: all markers show the check mark (an error keeps its mark), no step is current, and the compact summary reads the last step as completed with a full bar.

options.name: busy
options.description: The current step is working: its marker shows a progress ring in place of its number (still when animations are off) and TalkBack adds "in progress" (labels.busy). Ignored when finished.

states.name: complete
states.description: A filled accent marker with a check mark; the line after it is in the accent color.

states.name: current
states.description: An accent-bordered marker with the number and a tinted ring; the name is semibold.

states.name: upcoming
states.description: A bordered marker with the number; the name is muted.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger-tinted marker with an exclamation mark; the name is in the danger color. Takes precedence over every other state.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With onSelect, a step whose enabled is false is not a button, is marked disabled for TalkBack and its name is in the disabled text color.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A selectable step shows the Material ripple, clipped to the medium corner radius, while pressed.

states.name: compact
states.description: "Step 2 of 5", the name of the current step and a progress bar filled up to the current step.

appearance: Markers are circles 28dp across, grown with the font scale. The accent roles color the current and finished steps, the danger roles a step with an error, the strong border and muted text an upcoming step, on the surface background. The lines between steps use the default border color, or the accent solid color after a finished step. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Material 3 has no stepper, so the component is drawn by Monarch. The web switches to the compact form below a width of 36rem; Android, like iOS, measures the names on one line with a TextMeasurer and shows the compact form when the row does not fit the width, which also covers large font scales. The web step status override ('complete' or 'error') is the two flags complete and error; the iOS isOptional, isComplete, hasError and isDisabled are optional, complete, error and enabled, following the Kotlin convention of adjectives without 'is'. currentID and furthestID on iOS are currentId and furthestId. The web step label is any node; here it is a String. Hover underlining does not exist; the Material ripple is the pressed state. MonarchTone has no accent tone, so the accent color roles are used directly. The check mark and the exclamation mark are drawn with Canvas from the web's SVG paths, because Monarch bundles no icon set and the meaning must not depend on an app-supplied icon. Each step carries no interactionSource parameter, because there is one per step.
accessibility: The list of steps has the content description "Progress" (labels.progress), is a traversal group and carries collection info with one entry per step.

Each step is one TalkBack element. Its content description is the position, the name and the description ("Step 2 of 4, Team, Invite people"); its state description is the state ("completed", "needs attention" or "current step") followed by "Optional" for an optional step.
A selectable step has the Button role and a click action, and reserves at least 48dp by 48dp in the layout. The current step, upcoming steps not reached and disabled steps have no click action.
A disabled step in a selectable stepper is marked disabled.
State is shown by a check mark, an exclamation mark or the number, and by the weight of the name, not by color alone. Markers and lines are hidden from TalkBack.
The compact form is one element named "Progress" whose state description is the position and name of the current step; the bar is not read separately.
Names and descriptions wrap at font scale 2.0 and the markers grow with the font scale. Color changes animate with the theme motion and are immediate when animations are removed.
A selectable step draws the Monarch focus ring when focused from a keyboard or D-pad.
edgeCases: A horizontal stepper with compact Never squeezes the names of many steps into narrow columns, where they wrap; prefer Automatic on a phone.
With Automatic, a long description makes the row too wide and the compact form is shown.
A vertical stepper is never compact unless compact is Always.
furthest before current is ignored: the current step counts as reached.
In an unbounded width (inside a horizontal scroll) the row is never compact and the steps take their natural width.
Step identifiers should be unique; the identifier overload uses the first match.

examples.title: Wizard with clickable completed steps
examples.setupTemplate:
var current by remember { mutableStateOf({{current}}) }
var furthest by remember { mutableStateOf({{furthest}}) }
examples.setup:
var current by remember { mutableStateOf(1) }
var furthest by remember { mutableStateOf(1) }

examples.title: A vertical stepper whose reached steps can be selected
examples.setup:
var current by rememberSaveable { mutableIntStateOf(2) }
val steps = listOf(
    MonarchStepperStep(id = "plan", label = "Plan"),
    MonarchStepperStep(id = "team", label = "Team", description = "Invite the people you work with", optional = true),
    MonarchStepperStep(id = "billing", label = "Billing"),
    MonarchStepperStep(id = "review", label = "Review"),
)
examples.code:
MonarchStepper(
    steps = steps,
    current = current,
    furthest = 2,
    orientation = MonarchStepperOrientation.Vertical,
    onSelect = { _, index -> current = index },
)

examples.title: Always compact, with a step that needs attention
examples.setup:
val steps = listOf(
    MonarchStepperStep(id = "account", label = "Account", error = true),
    MonarchStepperStep(id = "billing", label = "Billing"),
)
